newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish firm Energoaparatura to buy back shares.
newsitem.headline: Polish firm Energoaparatura to buy back shares.

text.p: Polish engineering firm Energoaparatura SA will buy back shares from present stockholders and sell them to investors who bought shares at its last issue which a court did not register, the firm said.

Energoaparatura president Jozef Zajac told a news conference on Monday that his firm, which plans to enter the parallel market of the Warsaw bourse later this year, would conduct the operation by the end of July.

Zajac said Energoaparatura's 340,000-share series B issue last September had not been registered by a local court because the firm did not publish its issue prospectus in Poland's Economic and Court Monitor.
The Supreme Court backed the decision.
"After the court did not register the series B issue we propose that the 2,800 investors who bought those shares will receive shares of series A (from existing shareholders)," Jozef Zajac said.
Zajac said that this transaction would cost the firm 150,000 zlotys.

He said Energoaparatura's largest shareholders, the Polish- American Enterprise Fund, the Polish Private Equity Fund I and II and Polish Development Bank (PBR), would sell shares to the firm for 13 zlotys, last September's issue price.
Zajac added that at the next shareholders meeting on May 24 he would propose a new share issue for present shareholders so that none would lose out on the deal.
